text: Chapter one. What is the Scanner? Why automated screening beats gut feeling, every single time.

Here's the problem with manual trading. Most retail traders lose money because of three human flaws. Emotion, inconsistency, and analysis paralysis. You see a stock pumping, you chase it. It drops, you panic sell. Or worse, you spend hours analyzing and never pull the trigger. The scanner solves all three by removing YOU from the equation.

So what does the scanner actually do every day? It scans 116 tickers across US, Europe, and Asia Pacific markets. It detects the current market regime, whether we're in risk-on, risk-off, or something in between. It runs three screening strategies adapted to that regime. It scores each setup from zero to one hundred on four factors. It selects the top ten A-plus setups with entry price, stop loss, and profit targets. And it publishes everything automatically to the website, Telegram, and YouTube.

Let me walk you through the daily pipeline. First, it analyzes the market regime by looking at the VIX, S and P 500, dollar index, and treasury bonds. Then it runs a multi-strategy screen across all 116 tickers. The scoring engine assigns a composite score from zero to one hundred based on four factors. Next, safety filters remove any ticker with dilution risk or duplicates. The result is your top ten A-plus picks, each with entry, stop, and targets. Finally, everything gets published to the web, Telegram, and YouTube. Fully automated, every single day.

And here's the track record after 35 days of live trading. Total return: plus 5.46 percent. Maximum drawdown: just minus 1.63 percent. Win rate: 50 percent. And a profit factor of 1.7 times. That means for every dollar lost, the system made a dollar seventy in gains. Not bad for a fully automated system, right?

Quick quiz. Why can a 50 percent win rate still be highly profitable? Is it A, it can't, you need at least 60 percent? B, because average wins are larger than average losses? C, because losing trades are free? Or D, because the broker refunds your losses? The answer is B. With average wins of plus 10.3 percent and average losses of minus 6.95 percent, even a fifty fifty hit rate produces a 1.7 times profit factor. It's the SIZE of wins versus losses that matters, not how often you win.
Chapter two. Reading a Scan. Let's break down the anatomy of a daily scan and understand what every number means.

Every setup card has six key components. First, the ticker and strategy. That tells you which stock and which strategy flagged it, whether it's momentum, breakout, or pullback. Second, the score from zero to one hundred. A-plus means ninety or above, A means eighty-five to eighty-nine. Only A-plus makes the top ten. Third, the entry range. This is NOT a single price, it's a zone for placing realistic limit orders. Fourth, the stop loss. Your maximum pain point. If price hits this, you exit immediately. It's typically 5 to 8 percent below entry. Fifth, T-P-1 and T-P-2. Target price one is where you sell half. Target price two is where you sell the rest. And sixth, the risk reward ratio. How much you stand to gain versus how much you risk. Every setup requires a minimum of 1.5 to 1.

Let's look at a real example. B-T-U, today's number one pick with a score of 94. Entry at 39 dollars. Stop loss at 35 dollars, that's minus 10.3 percent risk. Target one at 46 dollars, that's plus 17.9 percent. And target two at 52 dollars, plus 33.3 percent. The risk reward ratio is 1.5 to 1. This is a breakout strategy play, meaning the stock is breaking above a key resistance level with strong volume confirmation.

The score comes from four factors. Technical analysis is worth up to 30 points. It measures R-S-I position, support and resistance breaks, and A-T-R expansion. Volume is worth up to 20 points. It looks at volume surge versus the 20-day average and O-B-V confirmation. Momentum is worth up to 25 points. It tracks the M-A-C-D signal, price velocity, and multi-signal conviction. And confluence is worth up to 25 points. It checks for insider buying, sector rotation support, chart patterns, and earnings catalysts. Add them all up and you get the composite score.

What's the difference between an A-plus score and everything below? An A-plus, ninety or above, means all four factors are strongly aligned. There are multiple confirmation signals, high institutional interest, and the setup makes the top ten picks. Anything below 85 means one or two confirmation factors are missing, volume may be weak, there's a higher risk of a false signal, and it gets filtered OUT before publication. We only show you the best of the best.

Here are today's top ten signals for March 30th. B-T-U leads with a score of 94, a breakout play. L-N-G follows at 93, a momentum play. E-Q-N-R at 91, breakout. V-L-O at 90, breakout. O-V-V at 89, breakout. C-T-R-A at 89, also a breakout. M-P-C at 88, momentum. H-E-S at 87, breakout. F-A-N-G at 86, momentum. And C-V-X at 85, breakout. Notice a pattern? In this early risk-off regime, breakout plays in energy dominate the top ten.

But before any ticker makes the top ten, it passes through two critical safety filters. First, the anti-dilution filter. This checks S-E-C filings for shelf registrations, active warrants, at-the-market offerings, and toxic fund involvement. Second, the anti-duplicate filter. This ensures no ticker appears twice in your portfolio simultaneously. Here's the key. A perfect score of 99 gets rejected if the ticker is already in your open positions. No exceptions.

Quiz time. A stock scores 96 but has an active A-T-M offering, meaning an at-the-market dilution program. What happens? A, it makes the top ten because the score is excellent? B, it gets a warning label but stays in? C, it is immediately rejected regardless of score? Or D, it goes into a special high-risk category? The answer is C. Dilution risk overrides everything. An A-T-M offering means the company can sell new shares at any time, crashing the price. No score can compensate for that structural risk. We learned this lesson the hard way with the INDO incident. A perfect technical setup that got crushed by dilution.
Chapter three. The three portfolio modes. Same signals, three different risk profiles. Pick the one that fits you.

This is the key insight that makes the scanner flexible. It generates the same ten signals every day. But HOW you use them depends on your risk tolerance. We run three model portfolios simultaneously. Growth, Calmar, and Conservative. Each uses different position sizing, rotation rules, and risk limits. Same signals, completely different outcomes. Let me show you.

Here's the comparison table. Growth mode is aggressive. It uses just 3 positions at 33 percent each, with a 5-day horizon and aggressive rotation. Best for experienced traders who can handle big swings. Calmar mode is balanced. 4 positions at 25 percent each, same 5-day horizon, aggressive rotation. This is the sweet spot for most traders. Conservative mode is the safe option. 20 positions at just 5 percent each, 10-day horizon, no rotation, and a maximum stop loss of 8 percent. Best for capital preservation.

Let's dig into Growth mode. Maximum firepower. It concentrates your capital into just three positions at 33 percent each. When a signal hits target two, you're making 33 percent times the gain. That's massive. But when it hits the stop, you're losing 33 percent times the drop. Painful. This mode uses aggressive rotation. If a better signal appears tomorrow, it replaces the weakest position immediately. Best for traders who can stomach 5 to 10 percent portfolio swings without blinking.

Calmar mode. The sweet spot. It holds 4 positions at 25 percent each. It's named after the Calmar ratio, which is return divided by max drawdown. This mode optimizes for the best risk-adjusted returns. In our 35-day live test, it delivered plus 5.46 percent return with only minus 1.63 percent drawdown. That's a 3.4 to 1 return-to-drawdown ratio. This is what we recommend for most traders. It's aggressive enough to generate meaningful returns, but disciplined enough to limit the pain.

And then there's Conservative mode. The sleep-at-night option. It spreads your capital across 20 positions at just 5 percent each. Maximum diversification, near-zero drawdown. In backtesting, it produced just minus 0.02 percent max drawdown. Essentially no pain at all. The tradeoff? Lower total returns. But if capital preservation is your absolute priority, this is your mode. It also excludes short squeeze strategies for extra safety.

You might wonder, how did we find these three configurations? We tested 98,000 parameter combinations using walk-forward validation. Eight dimensions: portfolio size from 1 to 20, number of signals used, minimum score filter, horizon length, strategy filter, rotation speed, partial take-profit, and trailing stops. The optimizer ran across 29 live scans with a 70-30 in-sample out-of-sample split, and identified the three configurations that maximize different objectives. Growth maximizes pure return, Calmar maximizes the Calmar ratio, and Conservative minimizes drawdown.

Quick quiz. You have 10,000 dollars and choose Calmar mode with 4 slots at 25 percent each. How much goes into each position? A, one thousand dollars? B, twenty-five hundred? C, five thousand? Or D, thirty-three thirty-three? The answer is B. Ten thousand divided by four positions equals twenty-five hundred per slot. That's your position size. And if the stop loss is 6 percent below entry, your maximum risk per trade is twenty-five hundred times 6 percent, which equals 150 dollars. That's just 1.5 percent of your total portfolio at risk on any single trade.
Chapter four. Signal lifecycle. From OPEN to CLOSED. Let's trace every possible outcome a signal can have.

Every signal has exactly six possible exit states. OPEN means the position is active and being monitored. T-P-1 Hit means you sell 50 percent and trail your stop to breakeven. T-P-2 Hit means you sell the remaining 50 percent for the home run. Stop Loss means you cut the loss immediately, no questions asked. Timeout means the horizon expired and you exit at market close. And Rotated means a higher-scoring signal replaced this position. Six possible endings, all pre-defined. No guesswork.

Let me show you a real winner. U-S-O, the oil E-T-F. We entered on March 6th at 105 dollars and 38 cents. Stop loss was at 99 dollars, a 6.1 percent risk. And what happened? In just 2 days, the price exploded to 119.63. That's T-P-2 hit. Plus 13.5 percent in 48 hours. Why? It was a breakout play and the Iran crisis sent oil prices surging. The scanner caught the setup, and the geopolitical catalyst did the rest.

Another winner. NOW, ServiceNow. We entered on February 27th at 105 dollars. The stop was at 95, a 9.5 percent risk. Five days later, the price surged to 121 dollars. T-P-1 hit at plus 15.2 percent. This was a pre-squeeze strategy play. Score 92. The stock had high short interest and when the squeeze triggered, the pop was explosive. Sold half at 121, trailed the stop on the rest.

Now a loss. Because losses happen. X-O-M, Exxon Mobil. Entered March 2nd at 159 dollars and 35 cents. Stop was at 149, but we didn't even get there. After just 2 days, a higher-scoring signal appeared, and Growth mode's aggressive rotation kicked in. X-O-M was replaced. Exit price: 151.35. Loss: minus 3.22 percent. Was that bad? Not really. The rotation freed up capital for a better opportunity. Sometimes cutting a mediocre position early IS the right move.

What happens when a signal times out? If price hasn't hit target one or the stop loss by the end of the horizon window, typically 5 or 10 days, you close at market price. Whatever it is. This is NOT a failure. C-R-M, Salesforce, expired at plus 4.94 percent after 5 days. A decent profit even though it didn't reach the target. Timeouts prevent you from holding dead positions forever. They force capital rotation into fresh opportunities.

Let's look at the full breakdown of our 46 closed trades. On the winners side, we had 16 T-P-1 hits with an average gain of plus 10.3 percent, and 7 T-P-2 hits. The best single trade was NOW at plus 15.24 percent. Average hold time for winners was 4.2 days. On the losers side, 20 stop losses with an average loss of minus 6.95 percent, plus 3 expired at a loss. Average hold time for losers was shorter at 3.1 days. The key takeaway? Wins are bigger than losses. That's how 50-50 becomes profitable.

Pop quiz. X-L-E is currently at 62.56 with target one at 63 dollars, only 0.7 percent away, and 4 days left on the horizon. What should you do? A, sell now and lock in the plus 11.2 percent gain? B, wait, it's 96 percent of the way to target one, let the system work? C, buy more to average up? Or D, move the stop loss higher? The answer is B. The system is mechanical for a reason. X-L-E is 96 percent of the way to target one with 4 days remaining. Let it play out. If it hits target one, you sell half and trail the rest. If it times out, you still exit with a solid 11 percent gain. Don't outsmart the system.
Chapter five. Position sizing and risk management. Let's talk about what a 25 percent allocation REALLY means and do the math together.

Position sizing in four simple steps. Step one, know your mode. Calmar equals 4 slots. Your allocation per position is 100 percent divided by 4, which equals 25 percent of total capital. Step two, calculate the dollar size. If your portfolio is ten thousand, each position is twenty-five hundred. With fifty thousand, it's twelve thousand five hundred. Step three, calculate your true risk. Entry 39 dollars, stop 35 dollars equals 10.3 percent risk on the position. On a 25 percent allocation, that's 10.3 percent times 25 percent equals 2.57 percent portfolio risk. Step four, check your comfort level. If 2.57 percent portfolio risk per trade feels too high, choose Conservative mode where 5 percent positions mean only 0.5 percent portfolio risk.

Here's the risk breakdown by mode for a ten thousand dollar portfolio. Growth mode at 33 percent means thirty-three hundred per position. With a typical 6 percent stop, you risk 200 dollars, or 2 percent of your portfolio per trade. Calmar mode at 25 percent means twenty-five hundred per position. Same 6 percent stop puts 150 dollars at risk, or 1.5 percent of portfolio. Conservative mode at 5 percent means just 500 dollars per position. Risk drops to 30 dollars, or 0.3 percent of portfolio. Choose based on how much pain you can handle.

Now here's a question people always ask. What happens after prices move? You bought X-L-E at 56.25 with a 25 percent allocation. Now it's at 62.56, up 11.2 percent. Your X-L-E position is now worth MORE than 25 percent of your portfolio because it grew. Do NOT rebalance mid-trade. The system tracks actual dollars, not percentages. When X-L-E closes, whether at target one, stop loss, or timeout, the freed capital goes back to the cash pool for the next signal. You only recalculate position size when opening NEW positions.

The T-P-1 split is one of the most powerful risk management techniques in the system. When price hits target one, you sell exactly 50 percent of your position. That locks in profits. The remaining 50 percent stays open, but with the stop loss moved up to your entry price, which is now breakeven. So even if the stock reverses completely from here, you keep your target one profit and lose NOTHING on the trailing half. And if it keeps running to target two? You double your gain. Heads you win, tails you break even.

Let's talk about maximum drawdown. It's the biggest peak-to-valley drop in your portfolio value during the test period. Our Calmar mode has a max drawdown of minus 1.63 percent over 35 days. That means the worst pain you'd have felt was seeing your ten thousand dollar portfolio drop to nine thousand eight hundred thirty-seven, before recovering. Now compare that to the S and P 500, which dropped 4.2 percent in the same period. The scanner's worst day is a normal Tuesday for the broader market.

Quiz time. You use Calmar mode with a twenty thousand dollar portfolio. B-T-U signal: entry 39, stop 35. How much money are you risking on this single trade? A, 800 dollars or 4 percent of portfolio? B, five thousand or 25 percent? C, 512 dollars or 2.56 percent? Or D, 200 dollars or 1 percent? The answer is C. Your position size is 25 percent of twenty thousand, which equals five thousand dollars. The stop distance is 39 minus 35, divided by 39, equals 10.26 percent. Dollar risk equals five thousand times 10.26 percent, which is 513 dollars. That's 2.56 percent of your total portfolio at risk on this one trade. Meaningful, but manageable.
Chapter six. Market regime detection. How the scanner automatically adapts to bull markets, bear markets, and everything in between.

The scanner detects five market regimes. Risk-On, when the VIX is below 18 and markets are in a strong uptrend. It favors momentum at 60 percent and breakout at 30 percent. Neutral, VIX between 15 and 20, flat market. All strategies weighted equally at 25 percent each. Early Risk-Off, VIX between 20 and 25, market turning down. Favors pullback at 35 percent and pre-squeeze at 40 percent. Risk-Off, VIX between 25 and 35, heavy selling. Pullback dominates at 50 percent. And Recovery, VIX above 35, markets reversing from a bottom. Breakout takes over at 50 percent plus momentum at 40 percent.

Right now, we're in Early Risk-Off. The VIX is at 27.4 and grinding higher. The S and P 500 dropped 1.74 percent on Friday. The dollar index is at 99.8, actually weakening which is unusual for risk-off. And the dominant strategy this week is breakout, particularly in energy names. This is why 7 out of our top 10 picks today are energy stocks breaking out above resistance levels.

Why does regime matter? Because running a momentum strategy in a risk-off market is like surfing in a hurricane. The scanner automatically shifts its strategy weights based on the detected regime. Right now, in Early Risk-Off, it favors breakout plays in energy and defensives. Sectors that thrive when fear rises. It would NOT push you into high-beta tech names that are getting hammered. The regime is the compass. The strategy is the map. You need both.

And the sector rotation confirms it. Look at this week's performance. X-L-E, the energy E-T-F, is up 11.2 percent. Gold, G-L-D, up 1.8 percent. Utilities, X-L-U, slightly positive. Treasury bonds, T-L-T, flat. Meanwhile, S-P-Y is down 1.7 percent, the Nasdaq Q-Q-Q down 2.4 percent, and A-R-K-K, the innovation E-T-F, down 4.1 percent. The scanner correctly identified this rotation and loaded up on energy. That's regime-aware trading in action.

Every scanner page and every status update shows the current regime badge at the top. Green means go aggressive with momentum plays. Orange means be selective, favor pullbacks in quality names. Red means maximum caution, only accept the strongest setups. And if you see purple Recovery, it means the bottom is likely in, time to load up on breakouts. Always check the regime badge before placing any orders. It tells you what kind of market you're trading in.

Quiz. The VIX spikes to 32 and markets drop 3 percent in a single day. What does the scanner do? A, stops generating signals because it's too dangerous? B, switches to Risk-Off and favors pullback plays in defensive sectors? C, goes all-in on momentum tech stocks? Or D, shorts the market? The answer is B. The scanner never stops. In Risk-Off mode with VIX between 25 and 35, it shifts to pullback strategies at 50 percent weight, targeting defensive sectors like energy, utilities, and gold. It looks for oversold quality names that have bounced off support. The scanner adapts, it doesn't hide.
Chapter seven. Getting started and convergence. Your onboarding timeline from day one to full portfolio alignment.

Here's your first week, step by step. Step one, choose your mode. New to trading? Start with Conservative. More experienced? Calmar is the sweet spot. Only use capital you can afford to lose. Step two, calculate your position size. Divide your portfolio by the number of slots. Ten thousand in Calmar equals twenty-five hundred per trade. Step three, subscribe to the Telegram channel for daily alerts. Or just check the status page every evening. Step four, place your first orders. Pick the top signals that match your available slots and use limit orders at the entry price. And step five, monitor and execute exits. When you get a T-P-1 alert, sell half. When timeout hits, close the position. Follow. The. System.

Let me explain the convergence timeline. Day zero, you start. Your portfolio is 100 percent cash while the scanner has been running for weeks. Days one through three, you build your initial positions from today's top ten signals. Days four and five, some positions hit target one, some time out, some stop out. Cash gets freed for new signals. Days six through eight, old positions continue to close and new ones open. Portfolio turnover accelerates. And by day ten, you're converged. Your portfolio now matches the model exactly. From here on, your returns should closely track what the status page shows.

This is the key concept. Convergence means your returns match the model. After about 10 trading days, roughly 2 calendar weeks, your actual portfolio will hold the same positions as the model portfolio. From that point forward, your returns should closely mirror what the status page displays. The first 10 days might differ because you're building up from zero while the model already had positions running. Be patient during the ramp-up phase. The system needs time to cycle through its first full rotation.

Convergence speed depends on your mode. Growth and Calmar both use a 5-day horizon, so you reach full convergence in about 5 trading days, roughly one calendar week. The faster turnover means quicker alignment with the model. Conservative mode uses a 10-day horizon, so convergence takes about 10 trading days, roughly two calendar weeks. Positions accumulate more gradually across all 20 slots. Either way, within two weeks you're fully aligned.

Before you start, let me warn you about the three most common mistakes. Number one, don't cherry-pick signals. If you only buy the ones you LIKE, you're adding your bias back in, defeating the whole purpose of automation. Number two, NEVER skip the stop loss. One runaway loss can wipe out weeks of gains. The stop is your insurance policy. Number three, don't change modes mid-week. Commit to one mode for at least a full cycle, then evaluate. The system needs time to prove itself. Switching constantly guarantees you'll miss the good trades.

Quiz. You started following Calmar mode 3 days ago. Your returns are minus 0.5 percent while the model shows plus 2.1 percent. Should you worry? A, yes, the system is broken, switch to a different mode? B, no, you haven't converged yet, give it 7 more trading days? C, yes, sell everything and wait? Or D, no, but double your position sizes to catch up? The answer is B. You're only 3 days in. Convergence takes about 10 trading days for Calmar. The model had existing winning positions before you started. Once your portfolio fully cycles through its first rotation, your returns will track the model. Patience is literally the edge here.
Chapter eight, your final chapter. Your dashboard and tools. The status page, Telegram, YouTube. Your complete command center for following the scanner.

The status page is your headquarters. Let me walk you through it. First, the mode tabs at the top. Switch between Growth, Calmar, and Conservative. Each tab shows its own equity curve, open positions, and performance metrics. Second, the performance panel. Total return, max drawdown, win rate, profit factor, all updated daily with live prices. Third, the orders section. This is critical. It shows BUY orders for vacant slots, ROTATE candidates if your portfolio is full, and WATCH signals that are overflow picks valid for two days. Fourth, the open positions table. Real-time profit and loss, days remaining, and visual progress bars showing how close you are to target one and the stop loss. And fifth, the trade history section showing every closed trade.

Let me decode the open positions table. A green badge means price is moving toward target one. You're on track, no action needed. An amber badge means price is near your entry, in the neutral zone. Keep watching. A red badge means price is approaching the stop loss. Prepare for exit. The progress bar shows your percentage of the way from entry to target one. 96 percent means you're almost there. Days remaining shows when the position times out. When it hits zero, you must close. And the scenario bar gives you a visual range from the worst case to the current price to the best case.

A-G-R-O, entered at 12.75, currently at 14.05, up 10.2 percent, 57 percent progress, 20 days remaining. S-M, entered at 29.75, now at 32.72, up 10 percent, 83 percent progress with 24 days left. And D-V-N, entered at 47.50, now at 52.07, up 9.6 percent, 83 percent progress, 20 days remaining. All four positions are green and moving toward their targets.

Telegram alerts make sure you never miss a signal. Every evening after the scan runs, you receive a message with everything you need for the next trading day. New buy orders for your vacant slots. Positions that need action, like an expiring horizon or one near its stop. The full top ten signals with scores and strategies. And a portfolio risk visualization. One glance on your phone and you know exactly what to do tomorrow morning. No chart staring required.

Here's what's inside your Telegram alert. A performance snapshot with daily return, drawdown, win rate, and profit factor. New buy orders with ticker, entry, stop, targets, risk-reward ratio, and allocation percentage. Action required alerts for positions that expired, hit stops, or need closing. Your open positions list with current profit and loss and days remaining for each. A portfolio risk bar showing a visual worst-case to best-case range. And the full top ten signals with scores and strategies. Everything in one message, every single day.

Every week, we publish a video retrospective on YouTube. It covers all the scans from the past ten days. Which signals hit their targets, which got stopped out, and the overall hit rate. The retrospective assigns a grade from A-plus to F based on two pillars. Pillar one is the setup hit rate, what percentage of signals reached target one or better. Pillar two is the portfolio simulation performance, how much the model portfolio returned. It's your weekly report card for the system's performance.

Here's how the grading works. A-plus means hit rate above 70 percent and portfolio return above plus 8 percent. Exceptional week, the system nailed it. A means 60 to 70 percent hit rate with plus 5 to 8 percent return. Strong performance. B-plus is 50 to 60 percent with plus 3 to 5 percent. Solid, above average. B is 40 to 50 with plus 1 to 3. Decent. C is 30 to 40 with 0 to 1 percent. Mediocre, the regime may not have fit the strategies. And F means below 20 percent hit rate with negative returns. Bad week, time to review what happened.

There's also a visual daily card that gets posted to Telegram every day. It shows the top three signals with Finviz charts, the current regime badge, portfolio status summary, and action items. All in one image you can check in ten seconds on your phone. Pin it, screenshot it, share it with your trading group. It's designed to be your one-glance morning briefing before the market opens.

And here's the golden rule. The single most important thing to remember. Trust the system. Don't override it with your feelings. The scanner exists precisely because human judgment fails under pressure. Place the orders, respect the stops, take the exits. In 35 days of live tracking, a 50 percent win rate with asymmetric risk-reward produced plus 5.46 percent return with only minus 1.63 percent drawdown. The math works. Let it work for you.

Let's wrap up with your complete scanner checklist. Pick your mode: Growth for aggressive, Calmar for balanced, or Conservative for safety. Calculate your position size by dividing your portfolio by the number of slots. Subscribe to Telegram for daily signal alerts. Place limit orders at the entry price, never chase. At target one, sell 50 percent and move your stop to breakeven. At timeout, close the position, no exceptions. At stop loss, exit immediately and protect your capital. Check the status page weekly to review performance. Allow 10 trading days for convergence with the model. And most importantly, never cherry-pick, never skip stops, and never override the system.

Final question. What is the single most important discipline for following the scanner successfully? A, picking only the highest-scoring signals? B, using Growth mode for maximum returns? C, following every signal mechanically without emotional override? Or D, checking prices every five minutes? The answer is C. The scanner's edge comes from consistency. If you cherry-pick, skip stops, or override exits, you're adding human bias back in. The exact thing the system was built to remove. Follow every signal. Respect every stop. Take every exit. The math does the rest. Welcome to systematic trading.
